_comment: digperiphs #6 (DMA) proof configuration: the Castalia defaults with the DMA0 configurable multi-channel single-shot DMA controller instantiated in the MUTEX page (page 2) sub-slot 8 (peripherals.dma=true, @0x6800), built with TWO channels (dmaChannels=2 -> the NCH generic; the register map is the 4-channel superset regardless, CH2/CH3 slots+bits read 0). DMA0 is architecturally two peripherals fused: an arbiter SLAVE register file @0x6800 (D4-xcollapse-clean like RTC/PWM/OW -- plain raw-strobe shim, no CAPTURE_CLOCK pre-latch) AND an arbiter MASTER (the transfer engine), the FIRST new arbiter master since the four harts. Enabling DMA is the ONE place the digperiphs program touches shared fabric RTL: the arbiter master count goes N=4 -> N=5 (the DMA is master index numHarts, the last slice), rippling through mp_arbiter (N=>5, MW=>3), resv_unit (N=>5), mutex_bank/irq_router (MW=>3), the sh_master decl (2->3 bits) and the arb_* buses (a 5th slice + the D18 lrsc/lock ties). Enabling DMA extends the IRQ source list to 119 per the A5 GLOBAL VECTOR RULE (vector 118 = DMA0_DONE combined channels-done, 119 = DMA0_ERR); NUM_EN_WORDS stays 4 (119 <= 128). Since QSPI0 and NFC0 are NOT in this default-shape config, only the UART0 RC trigger tap is live (trig_qspi0_rxf / trig_nfc0_rxf tie '0'); the wound config proves all three taps. Everything else is default (the NPU stays ON). Prove with: make verify CONFIG=config/castalia_dma.json
